thread:
sasha: Heads-up — seeing p99 latency jump on the gpt-small-quant fleet for requests with long context (> 4k). Spike started ~09:10 UTC.
marco: any profiler traces or flamegraphs yet?
sasha: grabbing a flamegraph now. initial quick look: big tail in attention kernels and a handful of huge microbatches that didn't get compacted. KV cache hit rate drops ~25% for these sessions.
jen: are those sessions sending huge max_tokens or unbounded streams?
sasha: most are chat-like with max_tokens=2048 and many prefix tokens. Some clients don't set a cap; default server-side is high. Also we saw microbatch sizes hitting 8+ when sequence lengths vary — bad for latency.
ryan: hmm. sounds like two problems: kernel selection for long seqs + batching heuristics for heterogenous seq lengths.
marco: can you paste the profiler snippet? we can check kernel choice decisions.
sasha: paste:
```
kernel: flash_attn (dispatch fallback to triton_fused for seq>4096)
avg_seq_len: 3600
microbatch_sizes_seen: [1,1,2,8,1,4,8]
p95_attn_ms: 45
p99_attn_ms: 190
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.74 -> 0.52 during spike
```
marco: flash_attn is great for small/medium seqs but degrades with very long seqs. maybe switch to cu_seqlen_opt for >4096 or force chunked attention.
jen: we should also protect tail latency by enforcing a server max_tokens cap and truncation policy. suggested defaults: max_tokens=1024 for hosted tier by default, timeout_ms=12000, truncation_policy=truncate_oldest.
oncall-runtime: deploy-bot: rolling restart canary to current runtime group? :thinking:
deploy-bot: @oncall-runtime noted. Deployment request queued; will run canary on 5% of traffic after CI passes.
ryan: For batching heuristics: implement dynamic microbatching that groups by seq_len buckets and caps microbatch at 4 for seq>2k. Also add a hard microbatch wall for latency-sensitive routes: max_microbatch=2.
marco: agree. And add a KV cache TTL sliding window change: increase per-connection cache budget so long-lived chat sessions don't evict frequently. That should recover hit rate.
sasha: quick config proposal (example):
```
runtime:
  default_max_tokens: 1024
  timeout_ms: 12000
  truncation_policy: oldest
  microbatching:
    max_microbatch: 4
    long_seq_threshold: 2000
    long_seq_max_microbatch: 2
  kv_cache:
    per_conn_budget_tokens: 65536
    eviction_strategy: lru-window
```
jen: also add p95/p99 SLO guards in the router: if p99 > 2x SLO, route new requests to cheaper lower-latency variant (e.g., smaller model or chunked-service) and mark for alerting.
ryan: what about request-level timeouts vs token caps? Timeouts prevent pathological tails quicker than token caps, but token caps guarantee cost control. We should enforce both: token cap first, fallback to timeout.
marco: agree. Order: 1) apply truncation policy, 2) enforce max_tokens, 3) apply timeout. That keeps semantics clear and reduces wasted compute.
sasha: running a local perf test with proposed microbatch limits + kernel override. Early results: p99 down from 190ms to ~95ms for attention stage on test harness, overall p99 down ~40%.
jen: nice. Any perf regressions from kernel changes elsewhere?
marco: need to run the perf matrix across seq lengths and batch sizes. I’ll kick off a matrix job: seq in [512,1024,2048,4096,8192], batch in [1,2,4,8].
oncall-runtime: matrix job started: job/permf-matrix-1763004321 (will post when done).
ryan: can we add a lightweight client header to indicate latency_sensitivity=true so we can apply stricter defaults for interactive routes?
jen: yes, but default should be conservative. Only opt-in for internal/PLG clients for now.
sasha: summary: - kernel override for seq>4096; - microbatch caps for long seqs; - server default max_tokens->1024; - truncation oldest; - enforce timeout 12s; - increase kv per-conn budget. Will open a PR with changes + perf numbers.
marco: please include regression matrix and flamegraphs in the PR. Tag me and oncall-runtime.
ryan: SGTM. thanks folks :thumbsup:
